  "rationale": "The added columns do identify intervenable treatments (seller_improvement_signal is an explicit settable action; mentioned_topics maps to configurable product/service levers), satisfying part (a) of the what-if claim. However, the set completely fails part (b): there is NO confounder among the added columns. A valid what-if design needs common causes of both the treatment (e.g., which improvement is pursued) and the outcome (satisfaction) to be adjusted for — for example product category, price tier, brand reputation, buyer expectations, or reviewer demographics, none of which appear. sentiment restates the outcome, and review_length_bucket is a mechanical text feature (mediator/noise at best, not a confounder). Because no confounders are present, none can be scored as named-or-unnamed, so the interventional counterfactual effect cannot be read off. The columns are reasonable as descriptive/attribution aids but do not realise a proper interventional design."
